content_preview.title: GitHub Actions Workflow Logs Get Secret Scanning in Public Preview, With No Backfill for Existing Runs
content_preview.summary: GitHub's secret scanning now reads Actions workflow logs after runs finish, but the Enterprise Cloud preview sends no alert notifications and does not scan logs created before it was turned on.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

GitHub secret scanning now covers GitHub Actions workflow logs, extending detection beyond the surfaces it already watched. According to a [GitHub changelog post](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-09-secret-scanning-detects-secrets-in-github-actions-workflow-logs/) published November 9, 2026, secret scanning "now detects secrets in GitHub Actions workflow logs, in addition to issues, wikis, discussions, and pull requests," and the capability is available in public preview.

editor_notes.source_verification: Read all three source snapshots in full from disk (gunzip'd .html.gz under sources/2026-11/github-actions-workflow-logs-get-secret-scanning-in-public-preview-with-no-backfill-for-existing-runs/): source-0.html.gz (github.blog changelog, 'Secret scanning detects secrets in GitHub Actions workflow logs', published Nov 9, 2026), source-1.html.gz (dev.to/leobaniak, 'GitHub secret scanning now reads your Actions logs, once the run is over', posted Nov 10), source-2.html.gz (dev.to/sascha-ms, 'Why Your GitHub Actions Logs Still Leak Secrets, and How to Stop It', posted Nov 13). Every direct quote in the article was checked verbatim against the raw snapshot text: 'now detects secrets in GitHub Actions workflow logs, in addition to issues, wikis, discussions, and pull requests', 'When a workflow run completes, GitHub scans its logs for provider patterns', 'available to enterprises on GitHub Enterprise Cloud with GitHub Secret Protection or GitHub Advanced Security, including those with data residency on GHE.com', 'disabled by default and applies only to repositories with secret scanning enabled under those licenses', 'Only workflow runs that complete after you enable the feature are scanned; existing logs aren't backfilled', 'generic patterns, custom patterns, AI-detected secrets, and secrets already masked by Actions', 'alerts from Actions workflow logs don't generate notifications during the preview...' (all source-0); 'only runs that complete after you enable it get scanned', 'alerts don't send notifications during the preview', 'treat each alert as a key that is already compromised' (source-1, Leo); 'logs of completed workflow runs for known provider patterns like AWS keys or GitHub tokens', 'off by default', 'only runs completed after enabling are checked, old logs are not', 'Base64 basic auth header, a signed JWT or a URL-encoded value', 'is new text the runner has never seen', 'there is no long-lived key that could leak' (source-2, Sascha Mirow-Stanitzok). All quotes match the snapshots exactly; no hallucinated or paraphrased-as-verbatim quotes found. Both dev.to writers are independent of GitHub (personal/team-lead authors, not GitHub staff or sponsored posts) — 2 of 3 sources independent of the vendor. github.blog and dev.to are both already on config/source_allowlist.txt; no allowlist action needed. Anthropic disclosure: not required - the article makes no mention of Anthropic, Claude, or any Anthropic-operated product in any passage.

No derived/computed figures appear in the article (no counts, sums, or ranks the Herald computed itself) and no disagreements between sources that needed reconciling.
